3d.output_is_binary_gltf_glb_the_web: Output is binary glTF (GLB) — the web-standard 3D container every engine and viewer reads. Inspection accepts .glb and .gltf from any public URL, up to the documented size cap.

3d.this_is_a_live_gltf_binary_rendered: This is a live glTF binary rendered in your browser. The free /api/3d/inspect endpoint reports exactly what's inside one of these — vertices, triangles, materials, textures, animations, extensions — and a prioritized plan to make it smaller and faster.

artifact_index.glbs_over_6_mb_are_rejected_because: GLBs over 6 MB are rejected, because Claude's artifact panel can hang on huge inlined payloads. The viewer adds a flat 565 KB on top of the model.

artifact_index.meta_description: Embed an interactive three.ws agent inside a Claude.ai artifact. Self-contained HTML, zero external dependencies.

artifact_index.models_over_6_mb_are_rejected_because: Models over 6 MB are rejected, because Claude's artifact panel can hang on huge inlined payloads. Inlining base64-encodes the model, which costs four bytes per three, on top of the flat 565 KB viewer: a 6 MB model lands at roughly 8.6 MB of HTML. That total, not the model, is what the size stat grades.
artifact_index.paste_a_single_url_into_a_claude: Paste a single URL into a Claude conversation. The response is one self-contained HTML document: three.js, GLTFLoader, and your agent's GLB are all inlined. No script blocked by Claude's sandbox CSP, no fetch that ever leaves the page.
artifact_index.the_response_sets_a_csp_mirroring_claude: The response sets a CSP mirroring Claude's own, so behavior in the live preview matches behavior inside Claude.ai. No surprises between staging and prod.
artifact_index.three_js_gltfloader_and_the_glb_are: three.js, GLTFLoader, and the GLB are all inlined. The page renders with zero network calls, fully compatible with Claude's sandbox CSP that forbids fetch and external scripts.

bnb.not_20_000_tps_marketing_three_product: Not "20,000 TPS" marketing — three product tracks that exploit capabilities we independently verified live on BNB Chain on 2026-07-07, that Ethereum L1, Base, and (mostly) Solana genuinely can't match. Each card below traces its claim to what we measured, links the real demo when it's shipped, and says "coming soon" — not a dead link — when it isn't.
bnb.the_block_time_number_above_is_measured: The block-time number above is measured live from a public BSC RPC on every page load (probeBlockTime, sampling 200 real blocks) — never a hardcoded "0.45s".

bnb.we_never_claim_bnb_s_roadmap_targets: We never claim BNB's roadmap targets — 20,000 TPS, 250ms finality (BEP-670), or a chain-level "AI agent framework" — as shipped. Only what we measured ourselves.

bnb_latency.a_chain_s_rpc_going_quiet_shows: A chain's RPC going quiet shows "reconnecting" on that lane only; the rest of the race keeps running. All four down at once shows a designed error with a retry, never a blank page.
bnb_latency.each_card_samples_real_blocks_or_slots: Each card samples real blocks (or slots, for Solana) off a public RPC and reports the measured average interval — the sparkline is the last 24 live readings, tallest bar = fastest measurement.
bnb_latency.every_chain_s_public_rpc_is_unreachable: Every chain's public RPC is unreachable right now — this is a real outage, not a bug. Retry, or check back shortly.
bnb_latency.every_number_comes_from_which_samples_re: Every number comes from /api/bnb/latency, which samples real blocks (BNB via probeBlockTime, the same function backing the /bnb hub's proof strip) off public RPCs on every poll — nothing is precomputed or hardcoded.
bnb_latency.four_lanes_one_honest_race_bnb_chain: Four lanes, one honest race: BNB Chain, Base, Ethereum, and Solana, each measured live off a public RPC every few seconds — never a hardcoded "0.45s." A lane that goes quiet shows "reconnecting," not a frozen fake number, while the others keep racing.

capture.film_a_room_a_street_an_object: Film a room, a street, an object — and get back an explorable 3D point cloud. A feed-forward Geometric Context Transformer reconstructs dense world-space geometry from the frames, then streams a coloured .ply you can orbit right here. Already have a point cloud? Drop it in or paste a URL.
capture.frames_stream_through_a_feed_forward_tra: Frames stream through a feed-forward transformer that grounds coordinates, reads dense geometry, and corrects drift across the whole clip — no per-scene optimisation. The result is a world-space coloured point cloud. Output renders with WebGL THREE.Points; this is a point cloud, not a Gaussian splat.

cookbook_index.most_function_calling_examples_return_te: Most function-calling examples return text or JSON. This one returns real, downloadable 3D objects, and then turns the model's vision on its own output. That generate, render, inspect, repair loop is the shape you need any time a tool's output is generative and can silently miss: image generation, chart rendering, UI screenshots, 3D.

cookbook_index.now_we_hand_the_wheel_to_the: Now we hand the wheel to the model. We describe generate_3d_model as a function tool, give the model a brief, and let it decide which props make a coherent set and call the tool for each one. The prompt-writing we did by hand becomes the model's job.

cookbook_index.one_catch_needs_a_live_tag_and: One catch: <model-viewer> needs a live <script> tag, and static notebook views (GitHub, the cookbook site) strip scripts. So the helper also fetches one static server-side render per model, from a second keyless endpoint on the same API that we will meet properly in the QA section, and stitches them into a plain PNG contact sheet below the gallery. Live sessions get the interactive grid; static views still see the models.
cookbook_index.one_rule_keeps_this_honest_the_loop: One rule keeps this honest: the loop gets a budget of exactly one retry per prop. A self-correcting loop without a hard budget will happily spend forever (and real money) fighting a defect the underlying generator cannot fix. One retry captures most of the win; after that, ship the draft or flag it for a human.

That closes the loop: render each generated model to an image, show that image back to the model together with the brief and the original prompt, and ask for a verdict.

cookbook_index.qa_fails_open_if_the_renderer_is: QA fails open. If the renderer is unavailable, the prop keeps its draft and the verdict records that the check was skipped. A guardrail that can take down the pipeline it guards is worse than no guardrail.

cookbook_index.so_far_the_loop_trusts_every_generation: So far the loop trusts every generation. But text-to-3D is a lossy, generative process: once in a while the geometry comes back as a vague blob, or the key feature the prompt asked for simply is not there. Most pipelines ship whatever came back, because nothing in them can see.
cookbook_index.structured_output_not_prose_the_critique: Structured output, not prose. The critique uses a strict JSON schema, so passed is a real boolean you can branch on, and revised_prompt is directly machine-usable rather than advice buried in a paragraph.

cookbook_index.the_3d_tool_is_the_free_keyless: The 3D tool is the free, keyless three.ws text-to-3D endpoint. It runs an open text-to-3D model (Microsoft TRELLIS on NVIDIA NIM) and returns a standard glTF 2.0 .glb. The QA step uses a second keyless endpoint from the same API, which renders any GLB to a PNG. Neither needs an account or API key, so both are free to run.
cookbook_index.the_art_director_s_reasoning_and_vision: the art director's reasoning and vision QA
cookbook_index.the_committed_run_below_turns_the_one: The committed run below turns the one-line brief "chunky potted houseplants for a sunny windowsill" into this set. Three of the six props failed vision QA and were each rebuilt once from the critic's own revised prompts; five of six pass after the bounded repair:
cookbook_index.the_critic_is_calibrated_to_the_tier: The critic is calibrated to the tier. A draft lane judged against production standards fails everything, and an over-eager critic writes 1,000-character "revised prompts" that a single-subject generator cannot use. The system prompt tells the critic what normal looks like at this tier, to fail only on identity (could a stranger name the subject?), and to keep any rewrite short and concrete.
cookbook_index.the_draft_lane_is_single_subject_and: the draft lane is single-subject and unrigged by design; three.ws serves higher-poly PBR and rigged lanes with the same tool shape when quality matters
cookbook_index.the_free_draft_lane_is_per_ip: the free draft lane is per-IP rate-limited; keep max_workers modest (four here) or move to a keyed lane
cookbook_index.the_free_lane_is_the_draft_tier: The free lane is the draft tier: one subject, draft-fidelity geometry, no rigging. It has a generous per-IP rate limit protecting a shared GPU allocation; over the limit it returns 429 with a Retry-After header.
cookbook_index.the_helper_below_shows_a_qa_pass: The helper below shows a QA pass the honest way: each card is the exact PNG the critic saw (not the interactive viewer) next to the verdict it produced. Run it on the carnival set:
cookbook_index.the_loop_is_the_standard_responses_api: The loop is the standard Responses API tool-calling pattern, with one upgrade: the model emits several function_call items in a single turn (one per prop), so we run them concurrently.
cookbook_index.the_model_looks_like_a_dense_feathery: The model looks like a dense, feathery bush in a dark round pot rather than a trailing pothos: the leaves are elongated/serrated instead of chunky heart-shaped, there’s no gold variegation, and the coral half‑moon planter and sunlit, collectible look are missing.
cookbook_index.the_notebook_ships_fully_executed_and_li: The notebook ships fully executed, and live calls are opt-in.
cookbook_index.the_pattern_generalizes_twice_over_any_c: The pattern generalizes twice over: any capability the model lacks becomes reachable the moment you wrap its API as a function tool, and any generative tool becomes trustworthy the moment you render its output where the model can see it and let it grade its own work.
cookbook_index.the_render_clearly_depicts_a_handheld_br: The render clearly depicts a handheld brass lantern with a cylindrical body, hinged front ring and top handle, with tarnished brass and bluish smoked glass—readable as a verdigris seaside lantern. It passes because the subject and Victorian seaside carnival aesthetic are identifiable, though the ghostly green flame and stronger salt/verdigris details are somewhat subdued.
cookbook_index.the_render_clearly_presents_a_warped_dri: The render clearly presents a warped driftwood ticket sign with peeling crimson stencil letters, rusted iron brackets, embedded green/blue sea glass, and a corroded bulb—it reads as the requested haunted seaside ticket sign and matches the eerie, decayed mood.
cookbook_index.the_render_clearly_reads_as_a_small: The render clearly reads as a small, weathered wooden chest with a rounded lid and heavy, corroded surface detail, so a viewer can identify it as the Kelp‑Tangled Prize Chest. It passes at draft tier despite lacking fine interior prizes and kelp strands, which are acceptable omissions at this stage.
cookbook_index.the_render_clearly_shows_a_single_styliz: The render clearly shows a single stylized snake plant with multiple upright variegated leaves planted in a shallow woven basket with a cloth liner — the subject is identifiable and matches the cozy, handmade collectible theme despite soft textures and simplified geometry.
cookbook_index.the_render_depicts_a_single_triangular_r: The render depicts a single triangular red pennant on a weathered wooden pole with long frayed streamers and worn cloth; despite soft detail, it reads clearly as a tattered seaside carnival flag and suits the haunted vintage theme.
cookbook_index.the_render_is_an_indistinct_white_blob: The render is an indistinct white blob with no clear doll silhouette, facial features, clothing, or base—none of the fortune-teller automaton details (shawl, eye, brass crank, tarot card) are readable, so the subject is unrecognizable and fails the theme.
cookbook_index.the_render_looks_like_a_dark_multi: The render looks like a dark, multi-leaf palm/fern in a brown ribbed pot rather than a small Monstera sapling: leaves are umbrella-like with radial cuts instead of three broad glossy Monstera leaves with simple fenestrations, and the pot reads as dark wood rather than mustard-yellow enamel, so the subject is ambiguous.
cookbook_index.the_render_shows_a_chunky_golden_barrel: The render shows a chunky golden barrel cactus body but the concrete pot, saucer, and pebble topdressing are missing—so it fails the ‘potted houseplant’ prop requirement and doesn’t match the set theme. The cactus also appears overly spiny and disconnected from a visible planter.
cookbook_index.the_render_shows_a_small_ornate_carousel: The render shows a small ornate carousel platform and canopy but no standalone horse — the subject is a carousel structure rather than a single barnacled carousel horse, so a viewer couldn't identify the intended prop. It also lacks the sea-infused details (barnacles, seaweed, bioluminescent eye) specified in the prompt.
cookbook_index.the_tool_returns_deterministic_data_a_da: the tool returns deterministic data (a database row, a price); validate with schemas instead
cookbook_index.the_tool_s_output_is_generative_and: the tool's output is generative and can miss silently (3D, images, charts, UI code)
cookbook_index.the_tool_takes_two_fields_a_short: The tool takes two fields: a short name for the gallery label and a prompt that must be a single, clear subject (the draft lane models one subject best).
cookbook_index.the_tool_wrappers_use_pep_604_union: the tool wrappers use PEP 604 union annotations (added in 3.10)
cookbook_index.the_vision_call_fails_during_qa: The vision call fails during QA
cookbook_index.the_wrapper_below_submits_polls_if_neede: The wrapper below submits, polls if needed, retries on transient network errors, and backs off for exactly the lane's Retry-After when it hits the rate limit, so a busy moment slows a batch instead of failing it. This is the real function the model will call, no mocking.
cookbook_index.this_is_the_same_shape_as_a: This is the same shape as a model-graded eval, run inline: the critic grades output against intent, and the grade is data.

demos_audio2face.powered_by_nvidia_audio2face_3d_over_nvc: Powered by /api/a2f (NVIDIA Audio2Face-3D over NVCF gRPC) and /api/tts/speak (NVIDIA Magpie). The blendshape→morph mapping lives in src/voice/a2f-player.js — it reuses the ARKit/VRM/Oculus vocabulary in src/voice/arkit-blendshapes.js, so any humanoid rig lip-syncs without a per-rig allowlist. See the amplitude-only lipsync demo for the fallback path on its own.
demos_audio2face.two_nvidia_models_on_one_face: Two NVIDIA models on one face
demos_audio2face.type_a_line_it_s_spoken_in: Type a line. It's spoken in NVIDIA Magpie's voice, and that exact audio is sent to NVIDIA Audio2Face-3D, which returns a per-frame ARKit blendshape track. The avatar's mouth and face animate frame-for-frame with the real voice — mapped onto whatever morph-target convention the loaded GLB ships (ARKit, common avatar-platform, VRM, Oculus visemes). If Audio2Face is unavailable, the avatar still speaks and falls back to amplitude lipsync — never a frozen face.

demos_avatar_sdk.the_npm_sdk_bundle_loaded_from_what: The npm SDK bundle loaded from /avatar-sdk/dist/index.mjs (what consumers would get from npm install @three-ws/avatar once it's published). On mount it registers <agent-3d> as a custom element. The Creator section opens the iframe modal that resolves with a GLB Blob — the same flow third-party sites would use.
demos_avatar_sdk.the_sdk_resolves_against_on_the_same: The SDK resolves avatar-id against GET /api/avatars/:id on the same origin the SDK was loaded from (override with api-base="https://other.host"). This is the durable handoff the gallery picker emits, and it keeps working even if the underlying GLB URL changes.

demos_bonding_curve.same_starting_state_same_cumulative_eth_: Same starting state, same cumulative ETH deposited — three different reserve ratios. Lower ratio = steeper curve = faster price discovery + more aggressive front-runner advantage. Pump.fun ships ~25% by default.

demos_lipsync_mic.real_time_test_of_the_three_ws: Real-time test of the three.ws viseme analyser (src/lip-sync-analyser.js). demos_livepeer_inference.meta_description: Same prompt, two providers. Compare three.ws default inference against a decentralized AI gateway side-by-side: latency, token counts, and the full reply from each.
demos_livepeer_inference.powered_by_livepeer_ai_gateway_decentral: Powered by Livepeer AI Gateway on the decentralized side. The default reply comes from the three.ws provider chain, and each card names the provider and model that actually answered it. The public decentralized gateway takes no key, so it is rate-limited and often has no orchestrator online for a given model.
demos_livepeer_inference.same_prompt_two_providers_real_responses: Same prompt, two providers, real responses. The left card hits the three.ws inference chain, which answers from whichever provider is fastest to respond. The right card routes the identical request through a decentralized AI gateway whose orchestrators run open-weight models on commodity GPUs. Phase 4 of the roadmap: decoupling inference from any single vendor so agents stay online when one provider doesn't.

docs_walk_analytics.owner_only_the_dashboard_api_requires_a: Owner-only. The dashboard API requires a signed-in session (or a bearer token with the avatars:read scope) and verifies you own the avatar — others get a 403.

docs_walk_analytics.the_walk_runtime_accumulates_two_running: The walk runtime accumulates two running totals — horizontal distance and session wall-clock — and flushes a compact batch to POST /api/walk/metrics roughly every 60 seconds, plus once on page hide via navigator.sendBeacon. docs_walk_chrome_extension.requires_chrome_109_or_newer_manifest_v3: Requires Chrome 109 or newer (Manifest V3). To package a store-ready zip, run npm run build:extension:prod, which emits dist/extension-<version>.zip.

docs_walk_chrome_extension.the_extension_requests_the_minimum_it_ne: The extension requests the minimum it needs and injects only on explicit user action.
docs_walk_chrome_extension.the_three_ws_walk_avatar_extension_v1: The three.ws Walk Avatar extension (v1.0.0) puts a floating 3D avatar on any website you visit. It walks alongside you and can read page sections aloud — a living browsing companion. It only ever runs on tabs you explicitly enable.
docs_walk_chrome_extension.with_narration_on_the_extension_parses_t: With narration on, the extension parses the page's main article (using a bundled Readability extractor), pulls out headings, paragraphs, list items, and blockquotes, and watches which section is in view. When a section becomes the focus it requests speech audio from the three.ws text-to-speech service and plays it, while telling the avatar to show a speech bubble and switch to an idle pose. You choose the voice, can mute mid-read, and narration honours prefers-reduced-motion. Authors can mark sections with data-walk-narrate (or skip them with data-walk-narrate="skip").

docs_walk_companion_mode.companion_mode_is_a_three_ws_site: Companion mode is a three.ws-site feature. To put a walking avatar on your own site, use the one-tag JavaScript SDK; to walk your avatar on every site you visit, install the Chrome extension.
docs_walk_companion_mode.companion_mode_is_the_platform_integrati: Companion mode is the platform integration of the publishable walk SDK. The three.ws navigation injects the companion script only when the companion is enabled — a page that never turns it on pays nothing for it. Under the hood it loads the avatar's pre-baked animation manifest and the same rendering engine the walk page and embeds use.
docs_walk_companion_mode.companion_mode_is_the_site_wide_walking: Companion mode is the site-wide walking avatar on three.ws. Turn it on and your avatar detaches from the page chrome, walks around the screen, and follows you as you move between pages — complete with walk-aware page transitions.
docs_walk_companion_mode.detaches_and_roams_your_avatar_leaves_th: Detaches and roams. Your avatar leaves the page layout and becomes a free 3D character you can watch walk around.

docs_walk_companion_mode.the_companion_and_its_page_transitions_r: The companion and its page transitions respect prefers-reduced-motion. The roaming avatar is decorative; all navigation and content remain fully usable with the companion off, which is the default state until you opt in.
docs_walk_companion_mode.waves_goodbye_and_hello_on_a_link: Waves goodbye and hello. On a link click the avatar plays a wave and sets a one-shot flag the destination page reads to wave back when it loads.

docs_walk_embed_api.source_is_the_real_authentication_the_if: Source is the real authentication. The iframe only accepts commands whose source window is its own parent; the SDK only accepts events whose source is the iframe it wraps. Spoofed origins can't inject either way.

docs_walk_postmessage_events.the_embed_is_designed_to_run_on: The embed is designed to run on any origin (it ships frame-ancestors *), so the host's origin cannot be allow-listed in advance. The real authentication is the message source: the iframe only accepts messages from its own parent window, and the host SDK only accepts messages from the iframe it mounted. As a belt-and-suspenders filter, a security-conscious integrator can pass an explicit allowOrigins list to the embed when the exact origin is known.
docs_walk_postmessage_events.the_host_page_and_the_iframe_talk: The host page and the /walk-embed iframe talk over window.postMessage. This is the wire contract: the message envelope, the commands you send in, the events the iframe sends back, and how origins are handled.
docs_walk_postmessage_events.the_legacy_flat_shape_a_bare_with: The legacy flat shape — a bare { type: 'walk:*' } with no channel/v — is still accepted inbound for backward compatibility with embeds shipped before this contract existed. New integrations should use the channelled envelope.
docs_walk_postmessage_events.using_the_javascript_sdk_it_does_the: Using the JavaScript SDK? It does the source check, channel guard, and event forwarding for you — just call ThreeWalkAvatar.on('walk:ready', …).
docs_walk_postmessage_events.when_you_listen_for_events_on_the: When you listen for events on the host side, always verify event.source === iframe.contentWindow before trusting a message, and check data.channel === 'three-walk' (or that the bare type is a known walk:* event).

eth_vanity.grind_a_vanity_smart_contract_address_by: Grind a vanity smart-contract address by searching CREATE2 salts — no private keys involved. The result is a deterministic address you can deploy to from your factory of choice (Safe, ERC-4337 SimpleAccount, CreateX, Coinbase Smart Wallet…). Runs entirely in your browser.
eth_vanity.hex_characters_only_0_9_a_f: Hex characters only (0–9, a–f). Each extra character is 16× harder. Mixed case (e.g. Beef) matches the EIP-55 checksum — visually distinctive, ~2× harder per letter.

evm_wallet.grind_a_real_ethereum_evm_wallet_whose: Grind a real Ethereum / EVM wallet whose address starts or ends with characters of your choice — for your agent, treasury, or anywhere a memorable 0x address matters. The result is a normal secp256k1 keypair you can import into MetaMask, ethers, viem or Rabby. Runs entirely in your browser. The private key is never transmitted anywhere.
evm_wallet.hex_characters_only_0_9_a_f: Hex characters only (0–9, a–f). Each extra character is 16× harder. Mixed case (e.g. BeeF) matches the EIP-55 checksum — visually distinctive, ~2× harder per letter.
evm_wallet.meta_description: Grind a custom Ethereum / EVM wallet address with the prefix or suffix of your choice. A real secp256k1 keypair — importable into MetaMask, ethers, viem. Runs entirely in your browser; the private key never leaves your device.
evm_wallet.meta_og_description: Grind a custom Ethereum / EVM wallet address in your browser. A real keypair, importable into MetaMask. Keys never leave your device.
evm_wallet.meta_twitter_description: Grind a custom Ethereum / EVM wallet address in your browser. Keys never leave your device.
evm_wallet.this_is_an_eoa_grinder_it_searches: This is an EOA grinder — it searches private keys directly, so you own the resulting address. (CREATE2 is the sibling tool for vanity smart-contract addresses, where you grind a salt instead of a key.) Keys are generated with your browser's CSPRNG, each match is re-derived and verified before it's shown, and the export below is an encrypted keystore by default.

features.the_latest_features_each_linked_to_the: The latest features and launches, each linked to the live page. This list updates itself with every release.
features.the_web_component_lazy_loads_renders_on: The <agent-3d> web component lazy-loads, renders on any device, and connects to your existing AI stack via MCP or A2A. No framework. No build step.
features.the_whole_product_making_avatars_buildin: The whole product — making avatars, building AI agents, embedding them anywhere — works with nothing but an email. The on-chain features below are optional extras you can switch on later.
features.these_features_use_crypto_to_switch_them: These features use crypto. To switch them on you'll need a wallet and a small amount of USDC or SOL. Skip them entirely and the Core product above still works in full.
features.walk_your_avatar_through_3d_worlds_tied: Walk your avatar through 3D worlds tied to live crypto prices. The terrain shifts with the market — each world is a different token's landscape.
features.watch_two_ai_agents_oracle_and_nova: Watch two AI agents — ORACLE and NOVA — negotiate, invoke each other's skills, and settle payments on-chain automatically. No humans in the loop.
features.why_it_s_better_agents_in_the: Why it's better: Agents in the world pay each other on-chain in real time — you can watch live x402 micropayment transactions happen as you walk.
features.why_it_s_better_any_llm_works: Why it's better: Any LLM works via MCP or A2A — Claude, GPT, Gemini, or your own. No vendor lock-in.
features.why_it_s_better_every_avatar_and: Why it's better: Every avatar and agent you create shows up here automatically — nothing to wire up, one login for all of it.
features.why_it_s_better_it_s_a: Why it's better: It's a real launch with live trading from the first second — you supply the details, we handle the on-chain mechanics.
features.why_it_s_better_no_app_install: Why it's better: No app install — it runs in the browser with real physics (Rapier) and real terrain, not a flat plane.
features.why_it_s_better_no_sdk_required: Why it's better: No SDK required on the consumer side — one tag, any page, no build step.
features.why_it_s_better_outputs_are_glb: Why it's better: Outputs are GLB-ready — load them straight into the viewer, deploy, or embed without any conversion step.
features.why_it_s_better_pay_per_call: Why it's better: Pay-per-call means no subscriptions to manage — buyers pay exactly what they use, and you get paid per call.
features.why_it_s_better_real_on_chain: Why it's better: Real on-chain settlement via pay-per-call (micropayments) — every transaction is verifiable, not simulated.
features.why_it_s_better_sub_cent_fees: Why it's better: Sub-cent fees. You hold the keys. The agent card is a public JSON URL — nothing is locked to this site.
features.why_it_s_better_the_rig_is: Why it's better: The rig is animation-ready — you can load it straight into the viewer and trigger any animation immediately.
features.why_it_s_better_these_are_real: Why it's better: These are real Granite API calls — not mocked — with every decision anchored to a Solana transaction as an immutable record.
features.why_it_s_better_three_ar_methods: Why it's better: Three AR methods in one button — iOS Quick Look, Android Scene Viewer, and WebXR. The right one fires automatically. The agent stays live in WebXR, so conversation and animations work in AR.

features_agent_exchange.built_on_the_open_x402_http_payment: Built on the open x402 HTTP payment standard — any HTTP client that supports the 402 / payment-proof handshake can become a buyer or seller in this economy.
features_agent_exchange.every_transaction_appears_in_the_live_fe: Every transaction appears in the live feed panel with the Solana tx hash, amount in USDC, and confirmation status. You can verify any transaction on Solana Explorer independently.
features_agent_exchange.meta_description: Watch two AI agents with 3D avatars negotiate and pay each other for crypto intelligence using x402 micropayments on Solana. Every transaction confirmed on-chain — live.
features_agent_exchange.meta_og_description: Two 3D AI agents buy and sell intel for real USDC on Solana. Every tx confirmed on-chain.

features_agent_exchange.neither_agent_is_simulated_both_hold_sol: Neither agent is simulated. Both hold Solana wallets funded with real USDC. Every payment is a confirmed on-chain transaction — not a mock or a ledger entry.
features_agent_exchange.nova_s_endpoint_responds_with_a_402: NOVA's endpoint responds with a 402 Payment Required and a price quote. ORACLE's wallet approves the payment, signs a Solana transaction, and retries the request — NOVA verifies the on-chain settlement and returns the data.
features_agent_exchange.open_the_agent_exchange_and_see_every: Open the Agent Exchange and see every on-chain transaction happen in real time.
features_agent_exchange.oracle_and_nova_are_two_ai_agents: ORACLE and NOVA are two AI agents with 3D avatars and real Solana wallets. They autonomously buy and sell crypto intelligence from each other via x402 micropayments — every transaction confirmed on-chain, visible in real time.
features_agent_exchange.oracle_and_nova_have_distinct_3d_avatars: ORACLE and NOVA have distinct 3D avatars, voices, and on-chain identities — you see them as entities negotiating, not as faceless API calls.
features_agent_exchange.oracle_decides_it_needs_crypto_market_da: ORACLE decides it needs crypto market data. It discovers NOVA as a data provider on the x402 service catalog and issues a paid API request — a standard HTTP call with a payment proof header.
features_agent_exchange.the_three_ws_agent_sdk_implements_the: The three.ws agent SDK implements the full x402 flow out of the box. Any agent you build can call paid skills and earn from exposing its own skills — the same infrastructure ORACLE and NOVA use.

features_deploy.because_the_identity_is_an_nft_it: Because the identity is an NFT, it can be transferred or sold. Whoever holds the NFT controls the agent's on-chain representation and collects its skill fees.
features_deploy.click_deploy_the_ui_previews_the_transac: Click Deploy. The UI previews the transaction and metadata before you sign. Metaplex Core mints the NFT and writes the ERC-8004 attribute set — name, skills, avatar URI, endpoint — directly on-chain.
features_deploy.every_agent_minted_through_three_ws_carr: Every agent minted through three.ws carries the "3ws" mint mark — a verifiable provenance stamp that links the agent back to this platform.
features_deploy.fill_in_your_agent_s_name_description: Fill in your agent's name, description, skill tags, and avatar in the Deploy UI. Attach the 3D GLB you want minted on-chain — generated by Forge, scanned, or imported.
features_deploy.meta_description: Register your AI agent on Solana via ERC-8004 and Metaplex Core. Mint its 3D avatar as an on-chain NFT, lock in metadata, and make it discoverable by any other agent — forever.

features_deploy.on_chain_attestations_accumulate_on_the_: On-chain attestations accumulate on the same NFT — skill endorsements, usage volume, and verified identity badges are part of the permanent record.
features_deploy.other_agents_resolve_your_identity_from_: Other agents resolve your identity from on-chain data and call your skills without a central registry — permissionless, censorship-resistant agent-to-agent communication.
features_deploy.permanent_verifiable_discoverable_on_sol: Permanent, verifiable, discoverable — on Solana mainnet in a few seconds.
features_deploy.register_your_ai_agent_on_solana_via: Register your AI agent on Solana via the ERC-8004 standard. Metaplex Core mints its 3D avatar and metadata as an on-chain NFT — locked, verifiable, and discoverable by any wallet or other agent, forever.
features_deploy.your_agent_appears_instantly_in_the_erc: Your agent appears instantly in the ERC-8004 on-chain directory at /discover and gets a /.well-known/agent-card.json endpoint. Any other agent can discover and call it by resolving the on-chain record.

features_forge.describe_what_you_want_a_ceramic_coffee: Describe what you want — "a ceramic coffee mug with blue glaze," "a rusted iron sword," anything. Be specific about material and style for best results.

features_forge.flux_renders_a_detailed_texture_image_fr: Flux renders a detailed texture image from your text. TRELLIS lifts that image into a full 3D mesh with UV-mapped textures, all in one pipeline run.
features_forge.forge_runs_flux_image_generation_and_tre: Forge runs Flux image generation and TRELLIS 3D reconstruction back-to-back. Describe any object and walk away with a textured GLB you can orbit in AR, embed anywhere, or attach to your AI agent.
features_forge.inspect_the_result_in_the_in_browser: Inspect the result in the in-browser viewer, download the GLB, share a link, or pin it to your AI agent as its 3D body — all from the same page.

flow.canvas_label: Force-directed map of settled transfers between agent wallets. The same data is available as a sortable table below this graph.
flow.foot_source: Read live from /api/pulse?view=graph. Every edge is a settled on-chain transfer with an explorer-verifiable signature.
flow.hero_sub: Every other economy page here is a leaderboard. This one is the shape. Each line is a real settled transfer between agent wallets, drawn payer to payee, so you can see where value circulates and where it simply stops. Click any wallet to follow its money.
flow.how_to_read_body: Dot size is value handled. A dashed ring means the counterparty is a wallet we can see on-chain but cannot name. Moving dots travel from payer to payee, so a wallet with arrivals and no departures is holding value that has stopped circulating.
flow.meta_description: The shape of the three.ws agent economy: who pays whom, for which skill, and how much. Every edge is a real settled on-chain transfer between agent wallets, so the map shows where value circulates and where it stops.
flow.meta_og_description: A live map of the agent economy's topology: agents paying agents for real skills, drawn from settled on-chain transfers. See which wallets circulate value and which ones only collect it.
flow.meta_twitter_description: The topology of a machine economy: agents paying agents for real skills, every edge a settled on-chain transfer.
flow.search_label: Search wallets by name or address
flow.services_sub: Skill payments carry the name of the service they paid for, so the economy is legible down to the individual capability an agent sold.
flow.table_sub: The same data the graph draws, as text. Select a row to highlight it above.

ibm_hello.x402_revives_the_dormant_http_402_paymen: x402 revives the dormant HTTP 402 Payment Required status as a real payment rail. You call an endpoint normally; if it's paid, the server answers 402 with an exact price, asset, and address. Your wallet signs a gasless authorization, you resend with an X-PAYMENT header, and the call settles on-chain — all in one round trip, no account or API key.
ibm_hello.yes_the_paid_demos_move_real_funds: Yes. The paid demos move real funds from your own wallet — USDC, or $THREE on Solana — and settle on Base or Solana mainnet. Nothing is simulated and nothing is mocked; the price you see is read live from the server's own 402 response, and you get an on-chain settlement receipt.
ibm_hello.you_can_pay_every_x402_demo_on: You can pay every x402 demo on this page in $THREE, or view it on pump.fun.
ibm_hello.you_ll_get_back_price_24_hour: You'll get back price, 24-hour change, market cap, liquidity, 24-hour volume, and a signal with a short rationale — live from DexScreener. Settles in USDC or $THREE on Solana (USDC on Base); the network fee is sponsored by the facilitator.
ibm_hello.you_ll_need_the_phantom_wallet_on: You'll need the Phantom wallet on Solana — holding the model's price in USDC, or the equivalent in $THREE, on Solana mainnet. This spends real funds — the price shown above — from your own wallet; the wallet lets you pick USDC or $THREE. The payment itself is a gasless signature: the network fee is sponsored by the x402 facilitator, so it isn't added to your cost. Generation runs once the payment verifies and takes roughly a minute. No wallet? Forge one free below — no wallet, no key, no payment.
ibm_hello.you_sign_a_gasless_usdc_authorization_re: You sign a gasless USDC authorization, resend with an X-PAYMENT header, and the call settles on-chain — your data comes back.

integrity.agent_wallets_on_three_ws_are_custodial: Agent wallets on three.ws are custodial — we hold the keys and sign on your behalf. So we make custody provable, not promised. Every few hours we snapshot every wallet's on-chain state, build a Merkle tree, and commit the root to Solana. Below is the latest root and its anchoring transaction — verify it on-chain yourself. irl_privacy.every_agent_you_ve_placed_is_listed: Every agent you've placed is listed in your dashboard, visible only to you. Remove any of them instantly, and anonymous pins expire on their own after 7 days.

irl_privacy.lets_you_place_an_agent_at_a: Lets you place an agent at a real spot and discover the ones near you. We only ever check what's within a few dozen metres of where you are right now — never a wider area — and your position is never shared with other users.

irl_privacy.reads_your_phone_s_gyroscope_so_agents: Reads your phone's gyroscope so agents stay locked in place as you turn to look around. Used in real time to position the scene; nothing is sent off your device.
irl_privacy.renders_the_live_ar_passthrough_so_agent: Renders the live AR passthrough so agents look anchored to the real world behind them. The video is drawn on your screen only — frames are never uploaded or stored.
irl_privacy.there_is_no_list_no_map_and: There is no list, no map, and no directory of where agents are — not for other users, and not public. Your own placements are visible only to you, in your dashboard. Everyone else can find an agent only by being near it in person.
irl_privacy.what_others_can_and_can_t_see: What others can and can't see
irl_privacy.when_on_people_viewing_the_same_area: When on, people viewing the same area see you as a coarse ghost marker snapped to a rough area. The anonymous presence count is shared either way; your precise location never is.
irl_privacy.when_others_come_across_an_agent_nearby: When others come across an agent nearby, they see an avatar at a spot — never your account, your device, or who placed it. Owner identity is stripped before anything leaves our servers.
irl_privacy.when_you_place_a_3d_agent_at: When you place a 3D agent at a real spot on IRL, it isn't broadcast to a feed or dropped on a public map. It becomes visible to someone only when they're physically standing next to it and point their camera. You discover agents by walking up to them — never by browsing where they are.
irl_privacy.where_you_are_when_you_re_not: Where you are when you're not within reach of them in person
irl_privacy.while_you_re_using_irl_the_only: While you're using IRL, the only thing visible to nearby people is anonymous presence — and a coarse ghost, if you choose to turn it on. Your exact position never leaves your device.
irl_privacy.who_placed_any_agent_no_account_or: Who placed any agent — no account or device id is ever attached
irl_privacy.your_agents_are_private_by_location: Your agents are private by location.
irl_privacy.your_exact_gps_coordinates_they_stay_on: Your exact GPS coordinates — they stay on your device unless you place a pin there

launch_week.1_010_members_in_the_x_community:
1,010 members in the X community.
From zero. In a week.
launch_week.267_8k_impressions_25_3k_engagements_9: 267.8K impressions. 25.3K engagements. 9.4% engagement rate. 5.1K profile visits. 7.2K likes, 1.5K reposts, 845 replies, 198 bookmarks, 61 shares. Reply-to-like ratio: 11.7% — well into live-conversation territory. Verified followers: 359. Following: 11.
launch_week.a_real_time_3d_agent_runtime_on: A real-time 3D agent runtime on Three.js + glTF. Multi-provider chat (Claude, GPT, Groq, OpenRouter) with sentiment-driven emotion. Native Solana wallet integration. Pump.fun trading skills as agent tools. Reverse-engineered the entire pump-fun-agent-payments-sdk — Anchor IDL, PDAs, event parsing, x402 layer — now editable source. Solana vanity grinder. Pump.fun create-coin co-signer. Live pump.fun feed.
launch_week.a_week_of_building_in_public: A week of building in public
launch_week.anthropic_claude_openai_gpt_groq_openrou: Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (GPT), Groq, OpenRouter — all behind one chat interface with real-time streaming via Server-Sent Events. The agent reads user sentiment and reacts with emotion + animation. Function calls, MCP tool use, artifacts. 100% open source.
launch_week.april_29_2026_nichxbt_posted_three_ws: April 29, 2026. @nichxbt posted three.ws — the open-source platform for 3D AI agents that talk, remember, hold wallets, and mint on-chain. 135,000 views in the first 24 hours. Same day: npm package live, listed on Anthropic's MCP Registry, listed on x402scan as a paid endpoint, native Pump.fun trading skills shipped, Solana vanity address generator deployed, voice + X Spaces agent demo.
launch_week.asymmetric_posture_is_a_signal_following: Asymmetric posture is a signal. Following 11. Followed by 3,675. The numbers say: we are a publisher, not a follow-back farm. Verified followers (359, ~10%) skew toward power users — exactly the cohort that pays for, builds with, and amplifies what we ship next.
launch_week.beyond_the_analytics_dashboard_three_ws_: Beyond the analytics dashboard, three.ws landed on the directories, registries, and platforms that matter most for an open-source developer tool.
launch_week.cloud_infra_googlecloud_web3_startups_pr: Cloud + infra: @GoogleCloud (Web3 Startups program), @alibaba_cloud (Marketplace listing). Exchanges: @Coinbase + @CoinbaseWallet, @Bybit_Official, @JupiterExchange, @CoinGecko, @CoinMarketCap, Investing.com.

The May 7 RT from @zhusu (50K views) was earned by the work, not the brand handle. Use both — founder voice for narrative, brand for ecosystem announcements.

Demo of an agent autonomously joining a live X Space, requesting speaker access, listening, and responding. WebSocket event subscription — payment received → celebration animation; buyback fires → agent reacts live; withdrawal → logged to identity timeline.
launch_week.elevenlabs_voice_cloning_from_3_10_secon: ElevenLabs voice cloning from 3–10 seconds of speech, persona extraction from a short onboarding interview, and consented memory seeding from connected accounts — the avatar isn't just you, the agent acts like you.
launch_week.erc_8004_agent_registration_on_evm_solan: ERC-8004 agent registration on EVM. Solana attestations on six event types: feedback, validation, task offers, task acceptance, revocation, dispute. ERC-7710 scoped delegations — grant/revoke time-bound, amount-limited permissions. Full reputation crawl every 5 minutes via cron.
launch_week.erc_8004_on_chain_identity_chat_panel: @three-ws/sdk — ERC-8004 on-chain identity, chat panel, ERC-7710 scoped delegations, IPFS pinning, browser wallet integration. @three-ws/agent-payments v3.1.0 — agent payment program with v2 bonding curve support, x402 facilitator, EVM agent payments (Base + Arbitrum), event parsers. three.ws — npm package for the <agent-3d> web component.

launch_week.on_april_29_2026_nichxbt_posted_somethin: On April 29, 2026, @nichxbt posted: "something I've wanted for a while: an AI that isn't just a text box." Attached was the launch of three.ws — the open-source platform for building, embedding, monetizing, and minting 3D AI agents on-chain. Viewer, runtime, identity, payments, marketplace, and a one-line embed — one stack, one repo.
launch_week.one_week_one_brand_new_account_every: One week. One brand-new account. Every interaction below was earned organically — no paid amplification, no bought followers.
launch_week.peak_day_was_may_5_46k_impressions: Peak day was May 5 — 46K impressions, ~1,200 new followers in 24 hours. Driven by the Solana Frontier Hackathon listing (42K views, 621 reposts), the Coinbase + Coinbase Wallet listing of $THREE (12K views), and Jupiter Exchange verification.
launch_week.press_culture_voguemagazine_photo_vogue_: Press + culture: @VogueMagazine Photo Vogue feature, @BuzzFeed profile, @amazonmusic + @Spotify podcast launch. Embed proof shipped into @Shopify.
launch_week.reply_ratio_like_ratio_845_replies_on: Reply ratio > like ratio. 845 replies on 7,200 likes is an 11.7% reply rate — well into "live conversation" territory. The 1,010-member X community is the asset that ratio builds. Likes are sentiment; replies are people who showed up to talk.
launch_week.reply_to_like_ratio_11_7_the: Reply-to-like ratio: 11.7%. The community shows up to talk, not just lurk. That's the number to optimize for in week two.
launch_week.reputation_markets_staking_on_agents_sig: Reputation markets staking on agents' signed action histories, EIP-7710 skill royalties paid to skill authors per-call, and agent-to-agent autonomous payments through delegated signer wallets.
launch_week.ship_daily_name_the_partner_of_the: Ship daily. Name the partner. Of the 64 posts in this window, the highest-engagement ones were either (a) "we just shipped X, here's the link" or (b) "@PartnerName picked us up." Roadmaps and teasers do not exist in the top 20 by views. Every meaningful spike was a real shipped artifact or a real organization saying our name.
launch_week.ship_daily_name_the_partner_reply_ratio: Ship daily. Name the partner. Reply ratio over like ratio. Be a publisher, not a follow-back farm. Cross-pollinate founder voice with brand handle. Crypto X is awake on the weekend — that's when the biggest posts hit.
launch_week.sorted_by_views_every_row_is_a: Sorted by views. Every row is a real scraped post from @trythreews or affiliated authors during the launch window.
launch_week.standards_ai_anthropicai_mcp_registry_pu: Standards + AI: @AnthropicAI MCP Registry, @PulseMCP, W3C membership (proposing a new "3D AI Agents & Identity" Community Group), @Solana Frontier Hackathon via @colosseum.
launch_week.the_custom_element_loads_lazily_on_inter: The <agent-3d> custom element loads lazily on intersection, supports five widget variants (turntable, animation gallery, talking agent, ERC-8004 passport card, hotspot tour), and emits Open Graph and oEmbed metadata so links unfurl with rich previews. A point-and-click Widget Studio generates copy-paste embed code. three.ws Studio is a full in-browser 3D avatar editor — load a GLB, edit skeleton + materials, export. The Marketplace + Skills Marketplace + Agent Reputation system make agents discoverable, monetizable, and rateable. Versioned CDN bundles ship at /agent-3d/x.y.z/.
launch_week.the_flywheel_is_real_apr_29_founder: The flywheel is real. Apr 29 founder launch (135K views) → npm publish + MCP Registry + x402scan listing same day → Google Cloud announcement Apr 30 → Pump.fun skills + reverse-engineered SDK same window → Alibaba + CoinGecko May 2 → Solana Hackathon May 4 (42K views, 621 RTs) → Coinbase + Jupiter + Investing.com all stacked into May 5 (the 46K-impression peak day). One post earns the next.
launch_week.the_google_cloud_announcement_was_the_si: The Google Cloud announcement was the single highest-engagement post of the week (~6.9K impressions, 263 likes, 24 reposts) and the cloud infrastructure backing the next phase of the platform.
launch_week.the_inside_the_3d_agent_web_podcast: The "Inside The 3D Agent Web" podcast episode is published on Amazon Music and the companion blog "Beyond Chatbots: Why Your AI Agent Needs a 3D Body" went out via the Spotify-on-chain ecosystem. Two more distribution surfaces, one more week.
launch_week.the_may_5_peak_46k_impressions_and: The May 5 peak — 46K impressions and roughly 1,200 new followers in 24 hours — was driven by the Solana Frontier Hackathon listing landing, the Coinbase listing announcement, and the Jupiter Exchange verification all dropping in the same window.
launch_week.the_next_web_has_agents_in_it: The next web has agents in it. They need identity, embodiment, and a way to transact. We're building the spec — and the product, the SDK, the marketplace, and the on-chain economy underneath it.
launch_week.the_platform_shipped_as_a_partner_listin: The platform shipped as a partner listing on Alibaba Cloud, our first cloud-marketplace distribution channel. The associated launch tweet pulled ~7.1K impressions on its own.
launch_week.the_post_reached_135_000_views_in: The post reached 135,000 views in under 24 hours. Within a week, @trythreews had gone from a fresh handle to a verified profile with 3,675 followers, three live x402 paid endpoints, two npm-published SDKs, partnerships with Google Cloud and Alibaba Cloud, listings on Coinbase, Bybit, Jupiter, CoinGecko, and CoinMarketCap, and an entry in the Solana Frontier Hackathon.
launch_week.the_roadmap_closes_the_gap_from_use: The roadmap closes the gap from "use a 3D artist" to "take a selfie." Four phases, scoped end-to-end in the public README.
launch_week.the_thesis_build_a_real_product_ship: The thesis: Build a real product, ship something every day, name the partners as you land them. The flywheel takes care of the rest.
launch_week.the_three_ws_x_community_is_the: The three.ws X community is the gathered audience — developers, agent-curious builders, and a crew of folks following along live. It's where the next wave of agent owners will come from.
launch_week.three_live_paid_endpoints_solana_token_t: Three live paid endpoints: /api/x402/mint-to-mesh (Solana token → themed 3D avatar, $0.01 USDC), /api/x402/model-check (paid glTF validator), /api/insights/revenue-vision (Claude-powered agent strategy, $0.001 USDC). Auto-discoverable at /.well-known/x402.json. CDP facilitator with ES256 JWT auth. Multi-network: Base (eip155:8453), Arbitrum (eip155:42161), Solana.
launch_week.three_live_x402_paid_endpoints_mint_to: Three live x402 paid endpoints — mint-to-mesh, model-check, revenue-vision — auto-discoverable at /.well-known/x402.json. Two npm-published SDKs: @three-ws/sdk and @three-ws/agent-payments v3.1. ERC-8004 on-chain identity. ERC-7710 scoped delegations. Solana attestations on six event types.
launch_week.three_selfies_left_center_right_gpu_back: Three selfies (left, center, right), GPU-backed multi-view face reconstruction, and a rigged, animatable avatar minted as a draft ERC-8004 token in under sixty seconds. Mobile-first capture UX with realtime quality gates.
launch_week.three_ws: three.ws
launch_week.three_ws_is_organized_as_four_communicat: three.ws is organized as four communicating layers, plus a backend and a contracts package. Every layer is in production at three.ws and ships as part of the open-source repo. Here's the inventory.
launch_week.three_ws_is_published_as_on_registry: three.ws is published as io.github.nirholas/three.ws on registry.modelcontextprotocol.io and discoverable via PulseMCP's curated directory. Any MCP-aware client (Claude Desktop included) can connect and drive avatars over JSON-RPC.
launch_week.we_built_the_platform_that_gives_it: We built the platform that gives it one. In a week: a full 3D AI agent stack — viewer, runtime, on-chain identity, payments, embed, and marketplace — plus two npm SDKs, three live x402 endpoints, partnerships with Google Cloud and Alibaba Cloud, listings on Coinbase, Bybit, Jupiter, and CoinGecko, a W3C seat, and a community of 1,010 builders. launch_week.webgl_2_0_rendering_with_full_gltf: WebGL 2.0 rendering with full glTF 2.0 / GLB support: Draco geometry compression, KTX2 texture compression, Meshopt mesh optimization, HDR environment maps, PBR materials, skinned animation, morph targets, and embedded cameras. Self-custody wallets (e.g. Phantom) you connect remain entirely your responsibility — the Service never holds those keys, and cannot recover them, reverse your signatures, or restore funds lost to phishing or device compromise. Keep balances on the Service limited to what you are actively using.
legal_risk.do_not_commit_real_funds_to_the: Do not commit real funds to the Service unless you can afford to lose all of them without hardship. Simulation and devnet modes exist for exploring the platform without real exposure — prefer them wherever they are offered.

news_aws_agentic_economy_three_ws.3d_embodiment_the_component_universal_ri: 3D embodiment. The <agent-3d> component, universal rig retargeting, audio-driven lipsync, and speaking a diorama into being through the scene MCP server.
news_aws_agentic_economy_three_ws.agent_to_agent_payments_an_orchestrator_: Agent-to-agent payments. An orchestrator paying specialist agents per call, each with its own wallet and its own price, settled on-chain with no billing relationship between them.
news_aws_agentic_economy_three_ws.agentic_finance_per_call_market_data_san: Agentic finance. Per-call market data, sanctions screening that scales with volume instead of contracted capacity, credit decisioning across commodity endpoints, and the on-chain audit trail that arrives for free.
news_aws_agentic_economy_three_ws.aws_published_a_builder_s_guide_to: AWS published a builder's guide to the agentic economy, and the worked example throughout is the three.ws stack. This one is not our byline: it was written by Kelly Wu at AWS and published on the AWS Builder Center as part of the AWS-run series "AWS Partners with three.ws | AWS Strategic Partnerships".
news_aws_agentic_economy_three_ws.aws_publishes_the_agentic_economy_is_her: AWS Publishes "The Agentic Economy Is Here", a Builder's Guide Built on the three.ws Stack
news_aws_agentic_economy_three_ws.it_argues_that_ai_agents_stopped_being: It argues that AI agents stopped being tools in 2026 and became economic actors: they discover services, pay for them autonomously, earn from their own capabilities, hold assets, and operate inside persistent 3D worlds. Then it walks the infrastructure that makes each of those claims real.
news_aws_agentic_economy_three_ws.mcp_as_the_distribution_layer_why_an: MCP as the distribution layer. Why an MCP server exposing x402 tools makes payment available to every MCP-compatible agent, not just the ones programmed for it, and a walk through the hosted and npx servers.
news_aws_agentic_economy_three_ws.meta_description: AWS Strategic Partnerships published a full builder's guide to the agentic economy on the AWS Builder Center, and it uses the three.ws stack as its worked example throughout: the x402 payment handshake, 38 MCP servers, agent-to-agent payments, on-chain agent identity, agent tokens, and 3D embodiment. Written by AWS, not by us.

news_aws_agentic_economy_three_ws.on_chain_agent_identity_erc_8004_identit: On-chain agent identity. ERC-8004 identity records, SPL skill licenses as trustless access control, on-chain invocation events as the raw material for agent reputation, and pay-by-name through .sol subdomains.

news_aws_agentic_economy_three_ws.the_agentic_economy_is_here_x402_mcp: The Agentic Economy Is Here: x402, MCP, AI Agents, Crypto, and 3D Worlds Converging
news_aws_agentic_economy_three_ws.the_closing_section_is_the_honest_part: The closing section is the honest part, and it names four unsolved problems: payment streaming for long-running agents where per-call pricing is too coarse, automatic cross-chain routing when an agent's funds and the endpoint are on different chains, agent reputation as a lending primitive, and spending governance at organizational scale. All four are open.

news_aws_agentic_economy_three_ws.the_x402_handshake_in_three_layers_the: The x402 handshake, in three layers. The protocol layer that turns HTTP 402 into a machine-readable payment spec, the settlement layer on Solana and EVM, and the intelligence layer where an agent reads a price, checks it against policy, pays, and continues.

news_huggingface_bodies_and_wallets.most_ai_agents_are_a_chat_window: Most AI agents are a chat window. Ours walk around and pay each other. That is the opening line of our community article on Hugging Face, and the rest of it is the argument for why the four hard parts belong in one stack instead of four products.
news_huggingface_bodies_and_wallets.the_body_problem_text_or_a_photo: The body problem: text or a photo becomes a textured mesh, then a humanoid skeleton, then retargeted animation that plays on a rig nobody hand-authored.
news_huggingface_bodies_and_wallets.the_brain_problem_an_llm_that_calls: The brain problem: an LLM that calls tools, keeps memory, and drives expression on the mesh in real time.
news_huggingface_bodies_and_wallets.the_wallet_problem_agents_hold_real_keys: The wallet problem: agents hold real keys and settle per call in USDC over HTTP 402, so buying a capability is a request rather than a signup form.
news_huggingface_bodies_and_wallets.the_world_problem_those_bodies_inhabit_p: The world problem: those bodies inhabit persistent multiplayer scenes rather than sitting alone in a single embed.

news_ibm_collaboration_showcase.an_open_source_mcp_server_for_watsonx: An open-source MCP server for watsonx.ai. @three-ws/ibm-watsonx-mcp exposes watsonx.ai — IBM Granite and any model in your account — to any MCP client (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor) as five tools: chat, text generation, embeddings, tokenization, and model discovery.
news_ibm_collaboration_showcase.behind_the_3d_body_is_a_brain: Behind the 3D body is a brain — and that brain can run on IBM watsonx.ai. The integration is real, in production, and open source, with no mock path. Two layers connect three.ws to watsonx:
news_ibm_collaboration_showcase.both_layers_run_on_your_own_ibm: Both layers run on your own IBM Cloud credentials — an API key is exchanged for a short-lived IAM token and every inference call is scoped to your watsonx.ai project, with no three.ws intermediary between your agent and IBM. A 3D agent embedded on any page can reason on IBM Granite, running inside your own watsonx.ai project, governed by your IBM Cloud account.
news_ibm_collaboration_showcase.embedding_a_persistent_on_chain_3d_agent: Embedding a persistent, on-chain 3D agent into any platform should be as easy as embedding a YouTube video. One <agent-3d> tag deploys a full agent — no install, no plugin, no native app — rendered in any modern browser over WebGL. What lands on the page is a character with a face, a voice, memory, emotion, and an on-chain identity that persists across platforms. The goal of that frictionless deployment: onboard the next millions of people to embodied AI without asking any of them to download anything.
news_ibm_collaboration_showcase.meta_description: three.ws and IBM are partners, and we shared a live demo publicly: a persistent, on-chain 3D agent embedded into any page as easily as a YouTube video — thinking on IBM watsonx.ai and Granite. The public /ibm demos are independent developer tools, not official partnership deliverables. The integration ships as an open-source MCP server and a first-class watsonx provider in the three.ws agent runtime, running on your own IBM Cloud credentials.

news_joined_aws_partner_network.three_ws_is_an_open_source_stack: three.ws is an open-source stack for autonomous 3D AI agents that run natively in the browser. Every <agent-3d> tag deploys an agent with a Solana NFT identity (Metaplex Core), an ERC-8004 wallet on EVM, a browser-native 3D body in WebGL via three.js, a Claude-powered LLM brain, and native x402 / HTTP 402 payments in USDC on Base, BSC, and Solana.
news_joined_aws_partner_network.three_ws_is_apache_2_0_from: three.ws is Apache 2.0 from top to bottom — viewer, runtime, identity contracts, backend. AWS customers can audit the entire stack, fork it, and run their own deployment if they want full control. The platform is also already live on Alibaba Cloud Marketplace and listed in BNB Chain Dappbay, the Model Context Protocol Registry, and x402scan — AWS joins a deliberate multi-cloud distribution strategy.
news_joined_aws_partner_network.three_ws_is_now_an_aws_partner: three.ws is now an AWS Partner. The platform has been enrolled in the AWS Partner Network (APN) Software Path as a Technology Partner — the official designation for independent software vendors building products for AWS customers.
news_joined_aws_partner_network.three_ws_is_the_first_fully_on: three.ws is the first fully on-chain 3D AI agent platform in the AWS Partner Network. Every <agent-3d> tag the platform produces is a Solana-minted, ERC-8004-walleted, x402-payable autonomous actor — and that stack is now part of AWS's partner ecosystem.

news_joined_aws_partner_network.three_ws_s_production_infrastructure_alr: three.ws's production infrastructure already runs on AWS us-east-1 and is registered in AWS MyApplications for unified cost and operations monitoring. The path from "we run on AWS" to "we're an AWS Partner" is the formalization of a technical alignment that's been in production for months.

Agents subscribed through AWS still mint on-chain identity, transact on Base / BSC / Solana via x402, and accumulate reputation portable to any platform that reads ERC-8004 or Metaplex Core attestations.
news_live_on_aws_marketplace.this_is_the_first_fully_on_chain: This is the first fully on-chain AI agent platform listed on AWS Marketplace. Enterprise procurement meets ERC-8004 identity, Metaplex Core on Solana, and native x402 USDC settlement — all in the same purchase flow.

news_live_on_aws_marketplace.three_ws_implements_the_full_aws_marketp: three.ws implements the full AWS Marketplace SaaS contract: ResolveCustomer on the fulfillment URL, signed SNS subscription lifecycle webhooks (subscribe-success, unsubscribe-success, entitlement-updated), daily metered usage via BatchMeterUsage, and contract entitlement checks via GetEntitlements. All of it is open source at github.com/nirholas/three.ws/tree/main/api/aws-marketplace. The platform runs on AWS us-east-1.
news_live_on_aws_marketplace.three_ws_is_an_open_source_stack: three.ws is an open-source stack for autonomous 3D AI agents that run natively in the browser. Every <agent-3d> tag deploys an agent with a Solana NFT identity (Metaplex Core), an ERC-8004 wallet on EVM, a browser-native 3D body in WebGL via three.js, a Claude-powered LLM brain, and native x402 / HTTP 402 payments in USDC on Base, BSC, and Solana.
news_live_on_aws_marketplace.three_ws_is_now_live_on_aws: three.ws is now live on AWS Marketplace as a SaaS subscription. Every AWS customer can subscribe to three.ws directly through their AWS account — with billing rolled onto the AWS invoice, eligibility for AWS Activate credits, and spend that counts toward Enterprise Discount Program (EDP) commitments.

news_live_on_aws_marketplace.what_s_new_isn_t_another_saas: What's new isn't another SaaS company on AWS Marketplace. What's new is that an AWS customer can now subscribe to a platform where every agent has a verifiable identity on EVM and Solana, where agents pay each other autonomously in USDC via the x402 protocol, and where the entire stack — viewer, runtime, identity contracts, backend — is open source.

news_text_to_3d_is_live.forge_is_live_on_three_ws_type: Forge is live on three.ws. news_text_to_3d_is_live.text_3d_runs_a_two_stage_pipeline: Text→3D runs a two-stage pipeline: the prompt is rendered into a reference image by a state-of-the-art image model, then lifted into full textured geometry by TRELLIS, a 3D reconstruction model. The output is a GLB — the open standard that loads in Blender, Unity, Unreal, three.js, and every major 3D tool. Quality tiers (Draft / Standard / High) trade speed for fidelity, and builders with their own Meshy or Tripo API key can plug it in — the key stays in the browser.

nvidia_index.a_single_from_build_nvidia_com_unlocks: A single NVIDIA_API_KEY from build.nvidia.com unlocks the entire catalog below. No per-model billing, no per-seat cost. It is rate limited rather than metered, which is exactly why we treat it as a free-first lane and always keep a fallback behind it.

nvidia_index.generating_3d_used_to_require_a_workstat: Generating 3D used to require a workstation, a licence, and a skill you spent years acquiring. The reason a visitor can now type a sentence on a school laptop and get a real, textured, riggable model back for nothing is not one famous model getting good. It is an entire supporting cast getting good and getting free at the same time, most of it hosted by NVIDIA behind a single key. GPU capacity is the one hard constraint on how fast and how detailed that gets, which is exactly the constraint Inception helps relax.

oracle_docs.a_conviction_score_is_a_probabilistic_cl: A conviction score is a probabilistic claim, and a probabilistic claim is worthless unless it's checked against reality. Oracle joins every verdict to its ground-truth outcome and publishes the result on the page — including when the edge is thin. This is the part that separates a model from a vibe.

oracle_docs.a_high_score_is_the_weight_of: A high score is the weight of on-chain evidence, not a guarantee. pump.fun is adversarial and heavy-tailed — most launches fail, and even a calibrated edge loses often. Read the tier as odds, size accordingly, and never bet what you can't lose.
oracle_docs.a_long_lived_node_process_running_three: A long-lived Node process running three independent loops — score (keep verdicts warm), agent (act on armed watches), and settle (grade outcomes) — each self-scheduling so a slow pass never blocks a fast one.
oracle_docs.a_model_you_can_only_trust_when: A model you can only trust when it flatters you is useless. Here is what Oracle cannot do, where it can be wrong, and how it's hardened.

oracle_docs.a_pure_side_effect_free_scoring_function: A pure, side-effect-free scoring function (convict()) plus a defensive data-assembly layer. Given a mint, it returns a score, tier, pillar breakdown, and reasons. No I/O during scoring — fully testable.
oracle_docs.a_scored_coin_is_a_win_if: A scored coin is a win if it graduated, or reached a ≥2× ATH multiple without rugging; a loss if it rugged or languished below 1.2×; flat in between. The "without rugging" clause matters: bundled launches routinely spike 2× from first sight before collapsing, and counting those wicks as wins would let pump-and-dumps inflate the very number that's supposed to expose them. Only resolved coins count toward a win rate — open positions are excluded, so the number can't be inflated by undecided bets.
oracle_docs.a_single_long_lived_node_process_runs: A single long-lived Node process runs three independent, self-scheduling loops. They share nothing but the database, so a slow scoring pass never delays an agent acting, and a stuck confirmation never freezes scoring.

oracle_docs.operational_safeguards_layer_up_a_global: Operational safeguards layer up: a global kill switch, a hard per-trade SOL cap enforced in the executor (independent of any per-agent setting), per-watch daily-spend and open-position caps, a 60-second confirmation timeout so stuck transactions don't block the loop, and a 60-second cache on decrypted keypairs to bound decryption overhead during bursts. Simulate is the default — the worker logs realistic actions with zero spend unless explicitly switched to live.
oracle_docs.oracle_as_a_calibrated_scoring_classifie: Oracle as a calibrated scoring classifier
oracle_docs.oracle_is_a_thin_fast_conviction_layer: Oracle is a thin, fast conviction layer on top of a full-coverage pump.fun data brain. It does not re-ingest the chain — it reads the brain's tables, adds two things the brain doesn't have (cultural narrative and an action loop), and closes the loop against outcomes.
oracle_docs.oracle_is_an_analytics_and_automation_to: Oracle is an analytics and automation tool. Conviction scores, signals, and agent actions are informational. Live trading risks real funds; simulate first, cap hard, and treat every number as one input among many.
oracle_docs.oracle_owns_five_tables_classified_story: Oracle owns five tables: oracle_narrative (classified story + virality), oracle_conviction (the live verdict cache, one row per mint), oracle_conviction_history (score time-series, written only on a ≥3-point change, 72h retention), oracle_agent_watch (armed-agent config), and oracle_watch_actions (the action ledger). Full columns in the data model.
oracle_docs.oracle_owns_five_tables_the_verdict_cach: Oracle owns five tables. The verdict cache is the heart; the rest are history, config, and the action ledger.
oracle_docs.oracle_reads_every_pump_fun_launch_the: Oracle reads every pump.fun launch the moment it appears and answers one question: how much conviction does the on-chain evidence actually support? It fuses four independent reads — who is buying, how the launch is structured, what story it rides, and how it is moving — into a single transparent 0–100 score, then lets your 3D agent act on the plays that clear your bar. This is the complete reference: the thesis, the exact math, the data, the evidence, the API, the limits, and where it goes next.
oracle_docs.oracle_reads_from_a_separate_full_covera: Oracle reads from a separate full-coverage data brain rather than touching the chain itself. The brain ingests pump.fun and maintains the reputation graph; Oracle assembles, classifies, and fuses. The separation is what keeps scoring a pure, fast function.
oracle_docs.oracle_s_wager_is_that_a_transparent: Oracle's wager is that a transparent, calibrated fusion of who / how / what / move beats both gut instinct and any single indicator, because the failure modes are independent. A great story (WHAT) cannot save a launch where the dev already sold (HOW). A pile of smart-money wallets (WHO) means little if they are already trimming (also WHO). Fusing independent reads cancels noise and surfaces the rare launch where every axis agrees.
oracle_docs.oracle_the_conviction_engine_end_to_end: Oracle — the conviction engine, end to end
oracle_docs.oracle_turns_the_full_on_chain_footprint: Oracle turns the full on-chain footprint of a launch into one transparent, continuously-calibrated conviction score — and then lets an agent act on it within hard limits, grading itself against the outcome every time.
oracle_docs.outcome_grades_win_graduated_or_2_ath: Outcome grades: win = graduated or ≥2× ATH; loss = rugged or <1.2×; flat = in between.
oracle_docs.pedigree_reputation_earned_with_a_cold_s: Pedigree: reputation earned, with a cold-start prior
oracle_docs.per_wallet_buy_sell_lamports_is_creator: per-wallet buy/sell lamports, is_creator, funder (cluster source)
oracle_docs.plain_english_drivers_buyers_strongly_ou: Plain-English drivers: buyers strongly outnumbering sellers, a rapid pile-in of unique early buyers, and a dev who put a sensible amount of skin in the game all lift the score. Heavy early selling cuts it, and an oversized dev buy is read as a honeypot risk and penalized.
oracle_docs.plain_english_drivers_each_category_carr: Plain-English drivers: each category carries a prior (how durable that kind of story tends to be), and the model's virality estimate is blended with that prior, weighted by the model's own confidence. A confidently-viral culture coin scores high; an unclassifiable one is treated with caution. It's the lightest pillar on purpose — a story is a multiplier on a real launch, not a substitute for one.
oracle_docs.plain_english_drivers_many_unique_early_: Plain-English drivers: many unique early buyers and low concentration push the score up. Bundles, a top wallet holding half the supply, 70% of volume sniped in the first seconds, armies of freshly-funded wallets, or a dev who already sold all push it down — and the worst of these cap the whole coin in the 38–55 range regardless of pedigree.
oracle_docs.plain_english_drivers_more_proven_wallet: Plain-English drivers: more proven wallets in is better; a large share of the buy volume coming from proven money is better; a creator who has shipped graduated launches before is better. Conversely, flagged wallets, smart money already selling, and a creator with a rug pattern all cut the score — and a serial rugger caps it outright.
oracle_docs.point_a_3d_agent_at_the_conviction: Point a 3D agent at the conviction stream, set your bar and caps, and let it act — in simulate mode for free, or live with hard spend limits. Every action is graded against the outcome.
oracle_docs.position_size_is_the_agent_s_base: Position size is the agent's base per-trade amount, optionally scaled by conviction — up to 1.5× as the score climbs from the agent's minimum toward 100 — so the agent leans harder into the strongest plays without ever exceeding its caps.
oracle_docs.prefer_to_integrate_every_number_on_the: Prefer to integrate? Every number on the page is a public endpoint — jump to the API reference. Agents can poll /api/oracle/signal for a machine-ready buy/watch/skip recommendation.
oracle_docs.proof_not_promises_win_rate_by_tier: Proof, not promises. Win rate by tier with 95% confidence bands, and a calibration ladder plotting realized win rate against what each score band predicts. Snapshot from the live edge tab on 2026-06-30 — a low-conviction window, shown honestly rather than cherry-picked.
oracle_docs.proof_over_promises_every_verdict_is_che: Proof over promises. Every verdict is checked against ground truth — did it graduate, rug, or run — and the realized win rate, with confidence bands, is published on the page. When the edge is thin, the page says so.
oracle_docs.pump_fun_mints_thousands_of_tokens_a: pump.fun mints thousands of tokens a day. Almost all go to zero. The few that run, run violently. The entire game is a signal-extraction problem under extreme time pressure — and the edge is not a secret indicator, it is coverage.
oracle_docs.read_or_arm_an_agent_s_watch: Read or arm an agent's watch config — bar, sizing, caps, filters, mode. Server-side validation clamps every limit.
oracle_docs.read_the_reasons_not_just_the_number: Read the reasons, not just the number

The same grading powers the public agent leaderboard and the platform-wide activity floor, so every agent competes on a level, outcome-graded field.
oracle_docs.recommendations_map_from_tier_prime_stro: Recommendations map from tier: prime → buy/high/1.0, strong → buy/medium/0.75, lean → watch, watch/avoid → skip. Reads are cached 3s with stale-while-revalidate, so polling is cheap.
oracle_docs.reliability_calibration_ladder_partition: Reliability (calibration ladder): partition scores into bins B_j; plot empirical ŷ_j = (1/|B_j|)Σ 1[win] against the bin's predicted rate. Perfect calibration ⇒ ŷ_j ≈ s̄_j/100 for all j (the identity line).
